consuming_facts.F1:

$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$,

consuming_facts.F2:
For $0\le\beta<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ the map $\Lambda_\beta$
with matrix $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero is a
proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $\det\Lambda_\beta=1$ and
$\Lambda_\beta^{-1}=\Lambda_{-\beta}$
([[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] (a)-(d)). For
$\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and
$\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$, the vector boost
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ has matrix $B^0{}_0=\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)$,
$B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)\beta_i$,
$B^i{}_j=\delta^i{}_j+\frac{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}\beta_i\beta_j$
for $\boldsymbol\beta\ne0$, and $B(\boldsymbol 0)=\operatorname{id}_V$; it is a
proper orthochronous Lorentz map with
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and for
$\boldsymbol\beta\ne0$ one has
$\frac{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}=\frac{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)^2}{\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta)+1}$
([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (i)).

consuming_facts.F5:
A spatial rotation $R$ of the frame fixes $e_0$, preserves the spatial
three-space $S$, satisfies $\delta(Rw,Rz)=\delta(w,z)$ on $S$, and its

consuming_facts.F1:
In the chart $x$, with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$,
$\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and $\varepsilon^{0123}=-1$, the electromagnetic
two-form has $F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$,
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; its Hodge dual
is $(*F)_{ab}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ with $*(*F)=-F$; for a
future unit $n$ the rest components are $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$ and
$b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$, one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$ and the reconstruction
$F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat=\eta(n,\cdot)$, the six
components $(e,b)$ determining $F$ at the event; for the laboratory rest
observer one has $e_i=E_i/c$ and $b_i=-B_i$, and the contractions are
$\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and
$F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$. The fields carry V m$^{-1}$ and T, and the
fractional structure is that of the frame's spatial Euclidean space
([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (a), (b),
[[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a), (b), (c),
[[def-em-fields]] (c), [[def-em-si-conventions]] (b)).

consuming_facts.F4:
Plane-wave data: $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex
amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$; the associated plane
wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] has wavevector
$\mathbf k:=Ks$ (so $|\mathbf k|=K=\omega/c$ and the propagation direction
$\widehat{\mathbf k}=s$), phase $\theta(x,t)=\mathbf k\cdot x-\omega t$ of class
$C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and amplitude equations
$\mathbf k\cdot e_{\mathrm a}=0$, $\mathbf k\cdot b_{\mathrm a}=0$,
$\mathbf k\times e_{\mathrm a}=\omega b_{\mathrm a}$ and
$\mathbf k\times b_{\mathrm a}=-(\omega/c^2)e_{\mathrm a}$; by
[[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (a) the pair is therefore a solution of the four
source-free smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations on
$\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] (a), (b), (c),
[[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (a), [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

consuming_facts.F5:

four-velocity $U_o=cn$, $n$ future unit timelike, that receives the wave reads
the angular frequency $\omega_n:=-ck(n)=-k(U_o)$ at the reception event of its

[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (ii)).

light rays are exactly the future null straight lines with coordinate speed $c$
in every inertial chart ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (i), (ii)).

consuming_facts.F6:
The exact classical Doppler theorem
[[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(vi) applies to the ideal wave
of [F4]: for inertial charts $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $|\beta|<1$ and frame-$x$
data $(\omega,s)$, it gives (i) the frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ with
$\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega>0$ and
$s'=\bigl[s+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot s)\beta-\gamma\beta\bigr]/\bigl[\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\bigr]$
(and $s'=s$, $\omega'=\omega$ for $\beta=0$); (ii) the reading
$\omega_o=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$ of an ideal observer of coordinate
velocity $w$, together with $\nu'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\nu$ and
$\lambda'=\lambda/[\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)]$; (iii) the longitudinal cases
$s=\pm\widehat\beta$; (iv) the two transverse protocols $\beta\cdot s=0$ and
$\beta\cdot s=|\beta|^2$; (v) the aberration relation
$\cos\theta_{x'}=(\cos\theta_x-|\beta|)/(1-|\beta|\cos\theta_x)$ with its
monotonicity; and (vi) its scope and exclusions. Its hypotheses — the adopted

consuming_facts.F1:
In the chart $x$, with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$,
$\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and $\varepsilon^{0123}=-1$, the electromagnetic
two-form has $F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$,
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; its Hodge dual

future unit $n$ the rest components are $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$ and
$b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$, one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$ and the reconstruction
$F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat=\eta(n,\cdot)$, the six
components $(e,b)$ determining $F$ at the event; for the laboratory rest
observer one has $e_i=E_i/c$ and $b_i=-B_i$, and the contractions are
$\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and
$F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$. The fields carry V m$^{-1}$ and T, and the
fractional structure is that of the frame's spatial Euclidean space

consuming_facts.F2:

amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$; the associated plane

consuming_facts.F6:
Orthogonality and norm conservation
([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]): $\eta(u,\Phi(u))=0$ for every
$u\in V$; if $U$ is differentiable on an interval with
$mU'(s)=q\Phi(U(s))$ for constant $m\ne0$ and $q$, then
$s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant; the conclusion holds verbatim for a
family of skew forms $F_s$ and their operators $\Phi_s$ with
$mU'(s)=q\Phi_s(U(s))$, with no derivative of $F_s$ required. Also,
differentiability at a point implies continuity there
([[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]), and a continuous real function on
an interval that never vanishes has constant sign ([[thm-intermediate-value]]).

For $0\le\beta<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ the map $\Lambda_\beta$
with matrix $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$,

linear part $\Lambda$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix ($\eta$-preserving,
$\det=+1$, $C^+$-preserving), and such a $\Lambda$ is invertible

([[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (i)-(iii)).

consuming_facts.F3:

matrix in $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $B^0{}_0=\gamma_w$,
